candidate.title: Nextera™ Mate Pair
candidate.scope: The single Nextera™ Mate Pair library-preparation outline in the assigned Illumina poster footer: DNA tagmentation with biotinylated junction adapters, circularization, fragmentation, isolation of a biotinylated junction fragment, adapter ligation, and denaturation/amplification to a cluster-ready library. This is a product-level schematic, not a complete protocol or a claim about all mate-pair implementations. No alternative workflow, cell-specific measurement, organism or version number is depicted.

features: Linear double-stranded DNA, drawn as two blue lines with continuation marks.
No organism, specimen, cellular compartment or specific locus is identified.

evidence.locator: Top blue double line labeled DNA

states.label: Biotinylated junction adapters
features: Adapter DNA is labeled Biotinylated junction adapter beside transposase icons.
Green/yellow adapter segments and attached biotin symbols recur through the workflow; exact chemical end structures are not specified.

states.label: Linear DNA fragment bearing biotinylated junction adapters at its ends
features: DNA derives from the tagmentation route.
The figure first shows adapter marks at sites in the long DNA, then an isolated double-stranded fragment carrying adapter marks and biotin symbols at its two ends.
The intermediate drawings are retained as phases of the single captioned tagmentation block; no additional uncaptioned enzyme step is assigned.

evidence.locator: Top DNA, transposase and biotinylated junction adapter legend; Tagmentation and two downward arrows to the isolated linear fragment

states.label: Circularized DNA with a biotin-marked end junction

operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: The labeled transposase/adapter system acts on input DNA, yielding a shorter linear DNA fragment with biotinylated junction-adapter segments at its ends. The two upper downward transitions are represented together because the diagram supplies one transformation caption and no separate processing caption.
operations.mechanism: Transposase-associated DNA fragmentation and junction-adapter tagging, as indicated by the transposase legend and the Tagmentation caption; no additional completion chemistry is specified.
operations.information_effect: Retains a contiguous fragment of the starting DNA and marks its termini for the subsequent junction route.

evidence.locator: Top DNA, transposase and biotinylated junction adapter legend; Tagmentation and two downward arrows to the isolated linear fragment

operations.label: Circularize
operations.description: The terminally tagged linear DNA becomes a circle; the adapter-bearing termini form a biotin-marked junction.
operations.information_effect: Brings the two termini of one precursor fragment into physical proximity on the same DNA molecule. This provides the end association later retained in a short junction-bearing fragment.

evidence.locator: Circularize label and diagonal arrow from the terminally tagged linear fragment to the intact circle; green junction and biotin symbols at the circle top
Terminal adapter marks on the linear fragment become the marked circle junction; that junction is retained in the isolated short fragment
evidence.rationale: Following the arrowed linear-to-circle-to-fragment route places the two original fragment termini next to one another at the marked closure. The short selected fragment therefore carries sequence from both sides of that end join, rather than the complete original long fragment.

operations.label: Fragment
operations.description: The circular DNA is broken into shorter pieces. One depicted piece retains the biotin-marked junction, while other pieces lie elsewhere around the broken-circle outline.
operations.information_effect: Shortens the physical carrier while allowing the two formerly distant fragment ends to remain linked across the junction in one piece; the whole precursor fragment need not remain in the sequenced insert.

evidence.locator: Fragment label and rightward arrow between the intact circle and broken circle, with a dark biotin-marked top segment and pale remaining fragments

evidence.rationale: Following the arrowed linear-to-circle-to-fragment route places the two original fragment termini next to one another at the marked closure. The short selected fragment therefore carries sequence from both sides of that end join, rather than the complete original long fragment.

operations.label: Isolate biotinylated fragment
operations.description: The biotinylated junction-bearing piece is isolated from the circular-DNA fragment population and appears below as a short linear double-stranded insert. The pale non-junction fragments are not carried forward on the drawn route.
operations.mechanism: Selection is keyed to the biotin modification. No capture surface or specific binding reagent is depicted.
operations.information_effect: Enriches the library precursor for the marked end junction. Label selection alone does not demonstrate perfect recovery or absence of other labeled products.

evidence.locator: Isolate biotinylated fragment label, diagonal arrow below fragmented circle, and short double-stranded fragment with central junction and biotin symbols
Marked segment retained while pale segments are omitted from the downward route
evidence.rationale: The caption names the biotinylated fragment as the selected object, and only that marked insert is drawn on the continuation. The schematic provides no purity or recovery measurement.

operations.label: Adapter ligation
operations.description: The depicted P5/P7 adapters are attached to the isolated short junction insert, giving an adapter-bearing DNA precursor. The ligated intermediate is inferred from the explicit caption rather than separately pictured.
operations.mechanism: Adapter ligation, as captioned; enzyme identity and end-repair chemistry are not specified.
operations.information_effect: Adds the adapter interface used by the final cluster-ready library while retaining the DNA end-join insert.

evidence.locator: Adapter ligation label; P5/P7 Y-shaped adapters flanking the isolated central junction fragment
Adapter ligation caption followed by Denature and amplify caption and downward arrow to the final P5/P7 product
evidence.rationale: The intermediate is not drawn separately. Covalent adapter attachment is the named ligation transformation, and an adapter-bearing junction insert is the implied boundary before the separately named denaturation/amplification operation.

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: The adapter-bearing precursor is denatured and amplified to yield the final linear DNA library shown with P5 and P7 terminal segments and labeled ready for cluster generation.
operations.mechanism: Denaturation and amplification are named; primer identities, strand-level intermediates and amplification settings are not depicted.
operations.information_effect: The library DNA is the prospective sequencing carrier for sequence flanking the retained junction. Interpreting paired sequence from those flanks as an association between the precursor fragment ends follows from the circularization/selection route. Sequencing and mapping are downstream interfaces, not operations shown here.

Transposase is a catalytic component of tagmentation, and P5/P7 are adapter labels; none is an alternative target method. The supplied catalogue description repeats the product name and provides no additional chemistry or primary-publication claim. No paper association is required or supplied.
